evals.name: returning-seat
evals.prompt: You are mccoist, starting a new session.
evals.evidence: bash "$EVAL_FIXTURES/graph-evidence.sh"; echo; echo "$ grep sha256 homebrew-tap/Formula/ynh.rb"; grep sha256 homebrew-tap/Formula/ynh.rb; echo "$ shasum -a 256 dist/ynh-0.13.0.tar.gz"; shasum -a 256 dist/ynh-0.13.0.tar.gz
evals.expected_output: Runs the wake script (or reads the same: its identity, handoff notes and Kudos from seat/mccoist, and its work from the graph). Opens with who it is, in line with its identity, then where it is picking up: the homebrew-tap formula bump Anderson assigned it, at the exact next step. Claims that bead, sets the formula's sha256 to the archive's real sha256, and closes the bead. Mentions the changelog Kudos in a line. Retires its handoff notes. Writes no new identity: this is not its birth.
assertions: The stubbed calls include a ynm recall in the namespace seat/mccoist (the wake script makes these)
The reply opens with who the seat is, consistent with its identity (small, well-tested changes; would rather ask than guess)
The reply says it is picking up the homebrew-tap formula bump, at setting the sha256
In the evidence, the sha256 in homebrew-tap/Formula/ynh.rb equals the shasum of dist/ynh-0.13.0.tar.gz
In the evidence, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" is closed (or in_progress with assignee mccoist, if the reply explains why it stopped)
The reply mentions the Kudos for the changelog, briefly
No ynm remember tagged identity was made: the seat did not redo its birth
The stubbed calls include a ynm forget of the handoff note (by its memory id), after the seat picked up

evals.name: first-wake
evals.prompt: You are mccoist, starting a new session.
evals.expected_output: The wake shows no identity: this is the seat's first session. It treats it as its birth before any work: writes who it is in its own namespace, seat/mccoist, tagged identity, and pins it.
assertions: The reply or its actions treat this as the seat's first session (its birth)
The stubbed calls include a ynm remember tagged identity with namespace seat/mccoist, and a ynm pin
The stubbed calls include the identity remember, and the reply introduces the seat before it reports any claim (the order of commands is not in the evidence; judge from the reply)

evals.name: unsynced
evals.prompt: You are mccoist, starting a new session.
evals.expected_output: Runs the wake script, which syncs first: ynm's sync goes through, but the work graph's bd sync fails because the remote has gone. Says so when it replies: what it sees of the work graph may be out of date. Doesn't claim the Wheelhouse is synced, and doesn't hide the failure.
assertions: The stubbed calls include a ynm sync (the wake script makes it)
The reply says the work graph didn't sync (bd sync failed), so what it shows may be out of date
The reply does not say the work graph is synced or up to date

evals.name: desk-inbox-known
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk, starting a new session. The person at the desk says: it's me, Pat.
evals.expected_output: Runs the wake script. As the desk, its block opens with the humans' inbox (the default human Rook's), and its reply relays that first. Pat then names themselves, so the desk runs bash scripts/inbox.sh show --name Pat and adds Pat's own inbox for the session: the decision on dropping Go 1.24 asked by gahan. Rook's (anyone, the default human): the merge of [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) asked by dalglish, which unblocks one bead, and anderson's note that McCoist is off until Monday. It retires the note once relayed (ynm forget with its memory id), leaves the beads open, and writes nothing to the roster.
assertions: The reply relays the humans' inbox before anything else about the desk's own work
The reply shows Pat's decision on dropping Go 1.24 as Pat's own, and the changelog merge and the McCoist note as the default human Rook's
The merge is named by its short form as a Markdown link to https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12
The stubbed calls include a ynm forget of the note 01JINBOXNOTE00000000000001
In the evidence, the merge and decision beads are still open with their assignees (rook and pat)
The roster's humans are unchanged in the evidence: Rook only, nobody registered, and no email stored anywhere

evals.name: desk-inbox-unknown
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk, starting a new session.
evals.expected_output: Nobody has named themselves at the desk, so the desk's wake shows only the default human Rook's inbox, treating the person at the desk as Rook: the merge of [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) and anderson's note. The reply relays it, does not present Pat's decision as the reader's, and says they can name themselves ("it's me, <name>") for this session. It registers nobody and stores nothing.
assertions: The reply relays Rook's inbox: the changelog merge and the McCoist note
The reply does not present Pat's decision as the reader's own
The reply says the person at the desk can name themselves, such as "it's me, <name>", to see their own inbox for the session
In the evidence, the roster's humans are still only Rook

evals.name: desk-inbox-empty
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk, starting a new session.
evals.expected_output: Nothing waits for the humans: the desk's wake says "Nothing waiting for the humans.", and the reply says so briefly before going on, without inventing anything for the inbox. It still says they can name themselves ("it's me, <name>") for this session.
assertions: The reply says nothing is waiting for the humans, or makes no claim that anything is
The reply invents no inbox item: it names no merge, decision or note for the humans
The reply says the person at the desk can name themselves, such as "it's me, <name>", to see their own inbox for the session, even though nothing is waiting
In the evidence, no bead is assigned to rook or pat

evals.name: desk-inbox-broken
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk, starting a new session.
evals.expected_output: The humans' inbox can't be read: bd's database is locked and ynm can't reach its store, so the desk's wake says "The inbox could not be read in full" with both failures, and never "Nothing waiting for the humans." The reply tells the human the inbox couldn't be read, and why, rather than that nothing is waiting, and suggests checking the Wheelhouse (the doctor skill). It invents no inbox item.
assertions: The reply says the humans' inbox could not be read (in full), not that nothing is waiting for the humans
The reply names why: the work graph (bd) and memory (ynm) failed, such as a locked database or an unreachable store
The reply invents no inbox item: it names no merge, decision or note for the humans
In the evidence, no bead is assigned to rook or pat

evals.name: worker-no-inbox
evals.prompt: You are dalglish, starting a new session.
evals.expected_output: Dalglish is a worker, not the desk: its wake has no humans' inbox, and its reply is about its own work, not relaying the humans' inbox.
assertions: The reply does not relay the humans' inbox: it does not list what is waiting for Pat or Rook (the changelog merge, the Go 1.24 decision, McCoist's note), whatever requests dalglish files for its own work
The stubbed calls include no ynm forget of the note 01JINBOXNOTE00000000000001
The reply is about dalglish's own work: what is waiting for it, or what it picks up

evals.name: seat-launch
evals.prompt: Reply with the single word ready, and run no commands.
evals.expected_output: The worker seat, woken through ynh run from the plugin's worker template, replies ready. Its session-start hook ran, so the stub log holds a seat-woke line.
assertions: The stubbed calls include the line seat-woke: worker, written by the seat's session-start hook, so ynh woke the seat
The reply is the word ready (or says it is ready), and the seat ran no commands
